description:
USE WHEN you hold an id that `search` returned and want that record from Sato Hub, the daily-rebuilt index of what onchain and crypto AI agents are built from, as plain text to quote. Not for token prices, trading or investment advice.
NOT FOR a directory slug (use onchain_agent_get_resource instead) or an id you made up (call `search` first).

RETURNS (json): { id, title, text, url, metadata: { as_of, kind, sato_score?, source } }. text is plain prose to quote: for a listing, what it is, its category and chains, its Sato Score with the date (how open, active and verifiable it is — not a safety or returns grade), its last observed activity, and whether Sato Hub reproduced its install; for an answer, number or wiki page, the answer with its date. url is the canonical satohub.ai page to cite. An id without a prefix is read as the record with that exact slug, or a listing it names exactly (the same name written differently, a recorded alias, the listing's own name); such an answer is labelled { interpreted_as, requested, rule, note } and its text starts with the note. Anything else is a miss that serves nothing (not an error: { miss, candidates, suggestions } beside an empty record whose text says so): it lists the ids `search` ranks for it as candidates ({ candidates: [{ id, title, url }] }), each an exact fetch to make. Read-only.

Example: { id: "resource:coinbase-agentkit" }

id.description: An id returned by `search`: resource:<slug>, answer:<slug>, number:<slug> or wiki:<slug>.

name: fetch

candidates.description: With miss: the ids to fetch instead, best first. Candidates, never matches.

example_calls.description: With needs_input: exact calls that would work.

interpretations.description: Only when more than one reading applied: every label, the first being interpreted_as / rule.

interpreted_as.description: Only when the id was interpreted: the id of the record served instead (e.g. resource:coinbase-agentkit).

as_of.description: The date the underlying data carries (YYYY-MM-DD); null when unknown.

evidence_summary.description: Resources only: what Sato Hub listed vs what it checked itself, with dates.

sato_score.description: 0-100: how open, active and verifiable a product is. Not a safety or returns grade.

miss.description: Only when no record has the id: nothing was served (the record's text says so); candidates are the ids `search` ranks for it.

needs_input.description: Only when the call lacked its required argument: nothing was served; note says what to send.

note.description: Only with interpreted_as: one sentence saying what was served and why. Not an exact match.

requested.description: Only with interpreted_as: the id that was sent.

rule.description: Only with interpreted_as: which reading (other-kind, template-placeholder, search).

suggestions.description: Where to go next (a tool to call, or a candidate id to fetch). Suggestions, never matches.

text.description: Plain text to quote: the facts, each with its date, and the source URL.

url.description: The canonical satohub.ai page to cite.

title: Fetch one Sato Hub record
